gaps.sentence: I couldn't use the meeting room because it ___ (clean) all morning.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive: was being + cleaned over a period in the past.

gaps.sentence: All the passwords ___ (reset) after last week's security breach.
gaps.hint: recent past, plural subject, present relevance
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: have been + reset for a recently completed action.

gaps.sentence: The ambush ___ (plan) by someone with intimate knowledge of the valley.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive (had been planned) stresses completion before the ambush; was planned is also acceptable.

gaps.sentence: They're getting the garden ___ (landscape) this spring.
gaps.explanation: Causative with get: are getting + the garden + landscaped.

gaps.sentence: The passengers ___ to fasten their seatbelts as the plane entered the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'The passengers were told to …' — passive of 'tell somebody to do'.

gaps.sentence: The results ___ (publish) on the university website next Friday.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle. 'Next Friday' fixes the future reference.

gaps.sentence: The escaped prisoner ___ (believe) to be hiding in the mountains.
gaps.explanation: Impersonal passive pattern: subject + is believed/said/reported + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: This machine ___ (NOT USE) for years before I repaired it.
gaps.hint: negative passive before a past point
gaps.explanation: The disuse continued up to the past repair: past perfect passive hadn't been used.
